title: Thy Way Is on the Deep, O Lord
description: Thy Way Is on the Deep, O Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 332, “God's Way is on the Deep”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy way is on the deep, O Lord! E'en there we'll go with Thee; We'll meet the tem-pest at Thy word, And walk up-on the sea.

lines: Thy way is on the deep, O Lord!
E'en there we'll go with Thee;
We'll meet the tempest at Thy word,
Poor tremblers at His rougher wind,
Why do we doubt Him so?
Who gives the storms a path will find
The way our feet shall go.
A moment may His hand seem lost,
O happy soul, of faith divine!
The love that kindles joy is thine,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
